query: High-entropy alloys can combine mechanical strength, wear resistance, corrosion protection, oxidation resistance, and thermal stability, while their large compositional space offers opportunities to tune degradation in harsh environments. Prior studies have largely considered wear and corrosion separately, and only a few reports address their combined action, leaving the governing behavior poorly understood. For a high-entropy alloy subjected to tribo-corrosion, what single mechanistic hypothesis could explain what governs the coupled response and why? Describe a controlled comparison that would isolate the governing cause, predict changes in total degradation and its wear and corrosion components relative to a matched baseline, state where the prediction should hold or fail, connect it to the available prior evidence, and identify a result that would falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: During aqueous tribo-corrosion of CoCrFeNiMn high-entropy alloy (HEA), the total material degradation rate is governed by one kinetic ratio:  R = (mechanical oxide‐removal rate)/(electro-chemical repassivation rate).  Owing to the high point-defect concentrations and multicomponent oxidation (‘cocktail’) effect, the HEA forms and self-heals a nanocrystalline Cr/Fe/Mn spinel-rich tribo-oxide up to ~3× faster than the same load removes it; therefore R < 1, the film remains intact and simultaneously suppresses both wear and corrosion.  If test conditions (load, speed, environment) are changed so that R > 1, the film is continually stripped and the HEA loses its advantage, converging on the behaviour of a conventional Cr-bearing stainless steel.
generation.material_initial_state: Solution-annealed, equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn HEA (grain size ≈ 20 µm, single FCC phase, Ra < 0.05 µm) and, for baseline, annealed 304L stainless steel with comparable hardness (≈200 HV).
generation.intervention: Pin-on-disk sliding of alumina counter-body against the alloy while immersed in aerated 3.5 wt % NaCl; normal load varied from 5 N to 25 N to tune the oxide-removal rate.
generation.conditions: Room temperature (25 °C), sliding speed 0.1 m s⁻¹, stroke length 5 mm, 10 000 cycles; tests performed at open-circuit potential (OCP) and at +200 mV vs Ag/AgCl to accelerate corrosion.
generation.structural_mediator: Self-generated nanocrystalline Cr–Fe–Mn spinel/passive layer (≈20–100 nm thick) that forms in the wear track.
generation.mechanism: High lattice distortion and high defect density in the HEA accelerate diffusion of Cr, Mn and O to the newly created surface, giving a rapid (sub-second) repassivation time.  When the mechanical removal rate is slower than this repassivation, the continuous tribo-oxide acts as a hard, lubricious, ion-blocking barrier, reducing both (i) direct asperity contact (wear) and (ii) anodic dissolution (corrosion).  The coupled degradation therefore collapses to the single parameter R.
generation.predicted_outcome: At 5 N load (R < 1) the HEA will show ≈40–60 % lower total material loss than 304L, arising from ≥30 % lower wear volume and ≥50 % lower charge density (corrosion) over 10 000 cycles.  At 25 N (R > 1) the advantage will disappear: HEA and 304L will exhibit similar total loss within ±10 %.
generation.baseline: 304L stainless steel tested under identical conditions; literature reports typical total material loss of ~1.0 mm³ and charge density ~120 mC cm⁻² after 10 000 cycles at 5 N in 3.5 % NaCl.
generation.boundary: The prediction is expected to hold only in oxidizing aqueous electrolytes that sustain passivation and under loads/speeds where flash temperatures remain below ~150 °C so the oxide does not spall.  It should fail in deaerated acid (no passive film) or at very high loads/speeds that keep R > 1 regardless of alloy chemistry.
generation.uncertainty: No quantitative data are yet available for the exact repassivation kinetics of CoCrFeNiMn; the estimated 40–60 % reduction is therefore uncertain to ±20 %.  Unidentified third-body abrasion or compositional inhomogeneity could confound results.

falsification_experiment.design: Run tribo-corrosion tests at 5 N and 25 N on both alloys while continuously monitoring (a) mass loss (wear track profilometry), (b) real-time corrosion current (potentiostatic hold), and (c) in-situ Raman/EDS mapping of the wear track to track oxide presence.  Calculate R from oxide removal rate (from wear scar growth) and repassivation rate (from current decay after potential transients).
measurements: Time constant of current decay after each load-unload cycle (s)
Thickness/coverage of oxide film in wear track (TEM cross-sections)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If at 5 N load (where R is measured <1) the HEA does NOT show ≥20 % lower wear volume AND ≥20 % lower charge density than 304L, or if oxide film is absent despite R < 1, then the hypothesis is falsified.  Conversely, if at 25 N (R > 1) the HEA still outperforms by >20 %, the hypothesis is also falsified.
